text:
Robert Thomas is in the middle of a four-game point streak, 2 goals and 8 assists, during which the Blues won 8-6, 5-2, 9-6 and 5-4. The Hockey Writers named him one of St. Louis's standouts of the week. It has been fun and chaotic, and it has lifted his season: 24 points in 24 games, 14 in his last ten.

The warning sign is big. St. Louis has scored 12.9 more goals than the quality of its chances deserves with Thomas on the ice. His own finishing is modest (5 goals on 6.2 expected), so it's his teammates converting at a pace that won't last. What's real is the engine: Evolving-Hockey had him 20th among forwards in value last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking said 79% of his exits leave the zone with possession and he ranked in the 94th percentile in primary shot assists. The Blues take 54% of the expected goals at five on five with him on. The 2019 Stanley Cup winner is driving play; the scoreboard is just overstating it right now.
headline: Robert Thomas and the Blues' run-and-gun week
